          <h1>Welcome to AffineDrift</h1>
          <p class="subtitle">AI-Assisted Golf Biomechanics Research</p>
        </div>

        <div class="welcome-intro">
          <p>
            This website at its heart is an attempt to build a website I would like to read. I am an avid golf researcher with an interest in robotics and the mechanics of linked systems. After scouring the web for resources I finally came to the realization that I could just build the website I was looking for with the articles and resources that I was trying to track down.
          </p>
          <p>
            Rather than trying to organize my notes offline across multiple devices and formats, why not collect them together in a unified place where others who are also interested can find value in them.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>



      <!-- Math Showcase -->
      <section id="framework" class="math-section">
        <h2>The Core Framework</h2>
        <p>The golf swing can be modeled as a control-affine system:</p>
        <div class="math-showcase">
          $$\dot{x} = f(x) + g(x)u$$
        </div>
        <p>
          Where <em>f(x)</em> represents the drift dynamics (passive forces like gravity and centrifugal effects) and <em>g(x)u</em> represents the controlled torque inputs from the golfer.
        </p>
      </section>

      <!-- About the Approach Section -->
      <section id="approach" class="approach-section">
        <h2>AI-Assisted Research</h2>
        <div class="approach-content">
          <p>
            Rather than curate the website myself, I have outlined articles and topics I would like to build or resources that I would like to see and then fed them to AI and importantly - iterated to improve quality. While much of AI generated golf content can end up as correlational gibberish, there can be significant value when you know how to use it right.
          </p>
          <p>
            Rather than asking it for answers, ask it to provide mathematical expressions that can be validated. Ask it to write code that can be reviewed. Ask it to track down sources and links for further information.
          </p>
          <p>
            The agents reviewing the site have different personas. There are editors attempting to improve the fluidity and prose. There is a curator coming up with new topics or avenues to explore. There is a librarian at work in the background curating a crosslinked bibliography. There are mathematicians and mechanics scouring the equations and validating them.
          </p>
          <p>
            Importantly, there are also critics. My goal here is not to hide weakness, but identify it and explore it. The edge cases and shortcomings of a given paradigm often hold extreme value.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>
